title: Chapter 233: Zhu Xiu
html:
“You found the killer?” Chen Ge sprang to his feet. “All right. I’ll be there as soon as possible!”

Chen Ge grabbed his jacket and rushed from the Haunted House. His first date had taken place inside a haunted school with a Red Specter. It had held neither excitement nor joy, but it had taught him the tragic history of a young woman: falling from a tall building, lying in a pool of her own blood, assailed by agony while death took its time claiming her.

She had watched her killer walk away, taking the truth with him. Her ballet shoes slowly turned red, and a kind young woman became a vengeful specter. Zhang Ya had shown Chen Ge everything, and he alone could speak for her. He took a taxi to the police station.

Ah Yong was waiting outside and recognized Chen Ge at once. “Inspector Lee is in the room on the left.”

“Thank you.”

Inspector Lee sat alone in the small office. “You’re finally here. Take a seat.”

Finding him alone gave Chen Ge a bad feeling. “Have you confirmed the killer’s identity? Didn’t you say there were still three suspects?”

“Yes, we’ve confirmed it. It’s him.” Inspector Lee took a photograph from a file on his desk. “His name is Zhu Xiu. He managed the equipment room at Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy and had little else to his name. He was also the headmaster’s youngest son and the ex-husband of the dance teacher, Sun Meijing.”

The photograph was a still from surveillance footage. It showed a thin man sitting at a roadside food stall, the filthy table crowded with beer cans.

“Are you certain?” Zhang Ya had once used the dance studio’s mirror to replay the original scene. Chen Ge had not seen the killer’s face clearly, but he remembered the man’s build. The figure in the mirror had been enormous, nothing like the thin man in the photograph.

“At first, he was only one of several suspects. We focused mainly on the academy’s physical-education and visiting teachers. But during our interviews, Zhu Xiu’s ex-wife, Sun Meijing, accidentally revealed an important detail.”

“What did she say?”

“She refused to discuss him, but we found a photograph she posted online years ago.” Inspector Lee showed Chen Ge a picture of a couple on his phone. The woman appeared ordinary but kept herself slim and fit. The man looked younger than her, yet he was enormous—perhaps one hundred and eighty kilograms.

“That is Zhu Xiu five years ago.” The man in the picture and the man in the surveillance still looked entirely different. “He lost roughly sixty kilograms in five years, which caught our attention. A deeper investigation revealed that he has no stable employment but spends heavily. Most importantly, he appears to be a hoarder.”

Inspector Lee produced another photograph. “After Zhu Xiu’s father died, Sun Meijing filed for divorce. She kept the house, and Zhu Xiu moved into a rental. We contacted his landlord and inspected the room under the pretext of repairing an electrical fault. It was filthy, cluttered, and reeked. Several pairs of women’s shoes were hidden beneath his bed.”

The last picture was taken in secret, and it captured the situation inside Zhu Xiu’s room.

“His job, build, and obsession all match. There’s a ninety-percent chance he’s the killer!” Chen Ge hissed. A man like that belonged behind bars, awaiting the law’s judgment.

“But all our evidence is circumstantial. He had the motive and opportunity, but that doesn’t prove he committed the crime. We need something concrete.” Inspector Lee rubbed his temple. “I have good news and bad news. Which do you want first?”

“Bad news,” Chen Ge said.

“Following the lead you provided, we discovered that all the girls who helped Zhu Xiu drive the victim to suicide have died under mysterious circumstances. There are no living witnesses.”

There was nothing Chen Ge could do about that. The witnesses Inspector Lee sought had been cursed into chairs, and one had been turned into candy and eaten.

“Without witnesses, you can’t charge him?”

“We can, provided we obtain concrete proof. But the case occurred four or five years ago, and almost all the physical evidence has been lost. More importantly, the coroner ruled the death a suicide, with no evidence of a physical struggle beforehand.”

“She jumped because he forced her to! That bastard cornered her at the window. It was murder!” Chen Ge had witnessed the scene himself in the mirror.

“That is not for me or you to decide. We need evidence.” Inspector Lee put away all the pictures. “Now, do you want to listen to the good news?”

“Okay.”

“Somehow, Zhu Xiu realized we were investigating him. He disappeared on the second day.” Inspector Lee removed the remaining photographs from the file.

“How is that good news?” Chen Ge did not understand. He turned toward the pictures on the desk.

“By refusing to cooperate and obstructing the investigation, he gives us grounds to take stronger measures, including requesting assistance from other precincts.” Inspector Lee continued explaining, but Chen Ge no longer heard him. He picked up one photograph, his eyes trembling. “Why is this picture here?”

Inspector Lee glanced at it. “That is the last picture we have of Zhu Xiu. Apparently, he disappeared inside this building.”

“Why would he go there?” Chen Ge narrowed his eyes. The photograph showed Building Three of Fang Hwa Apartments.

“We’re wondering the same thing.” Inspector Lee did not understand Chen Ge’s reaction. “Further investigation showed this wasn’t Zhu Xiu’s first visit to Fang Hwa Apartments. We reviewed surveillance footage from the past three months and found that he entered Building Three on three occasions. Curiously, every visit took place at midnight—specifically, at the end of Tuesday night.”

“How long does he spend there each time?”

“About ten minutes.”

“Can you give me an exact time frame?”

“He arrived around 11:50 p.m. on Tuesday and left shortly after midnight. No one knows what he was doing.” Inspector Lee shared his suspicion. “Perhaps he knew his crimes would eventually be exposed and was searching for an escape route.”

“After midnight on Tuesday, it becomes Wednesday.” Chen Ge set the photograph down. The number three kept recurring. He now suspected that Zhu Xiu had received a flyer from the Ghost Stories Society and had been trying—so far without success—to find them.

“Fang Hwa Apartments is now central to our investigation, but the city precinct is handling a major case and lacks the personnel to cover the entire building,” Inspector Lee explained. “We may have to wait several days. Don’t worry—finding him should be straightforward. Gathering enough evidence to convict him will be the difficult part.”

“I understand.” Chen Ge memorized all the pictures on the table in his mind. “Thank you, Uncle Lee!”

“Why are you thanking me? I’m only doing my job.” Years of experience told Inspector Lee that something was wrong with Chen Ge’s tone.

“Okay, if there’s nothing else, I’ll be leaving.”

“Be careful.”

“Don’t worry.”

After leaving the station, Chen Ge slipped a hand into his pocket and pinched the flyer between his fingers.

“After today, it’ll be Wednesday.”
